title: Sleep, Travel or Stay? A Parent Guide
endLine: Winter food runs short: animals travel, rest, or stay and change.

scenes.tts: Why does a cardinal stay when hummingbirds leave for winter? Use a card sort and a window watch to explore that with your child.
scenes.caption: Why does a cardinal stay when hummingbirds leave for winter? Use a card sort and a window watch to explore that with your child.
scenes.visual: Friendly schematic: a snowy Virginia yard seen through a large window frame. A red cardinal sits fluffed on a bare branch; a faint dotted outline of a hummingbird fades away over the horizon. Large text: 'Who leaves? Who stays?' No photos of real children.
scenes.narration: Why does a cardinal stay when hummingbirds leave for winter? Use a card sort and a window watch to explore that with your child.

scenes.visual: Same window and yard. Title 'Sleep, Travel or Stay?' appears for 2 seconds; light snow drifts down.

scenes.tts: Your child practices sorting with reasons and changing a guess when new evidence comes in. They also count what they see and compare seasons. This takes about thirty minutes, plus a fifteen-minute window watch.
scenes.caption: Your child practices sorting with reasons and changing a guess when new evidence comes in. They also count what they see and compare seasons. This takes about thirty minutes, plus a fifteen-minute window watch.
scenes.visual: The view moves to a table below the window. Three labelled sheets slide into place: 'Travel', 'Rest', 'Stay and change'. Three small labels appear one by one at the side: 'Sort with reasons', 'Change a guess', 'Count and compare'.
scenes.narration: Your child practices sorting with reasons and changing a guess when new evidence comes in. They also count what they see and compare seasons. This takes about thirty minutes, plus a fifteen-minute window watch.

scenes.tts: Draw, print, or cut out ten animal cards. Label them with these names. Ruby-throated hummingbird, monarch butterfly, tundra swan, groundhog, and bat. Eastern box turtle, wood frog, white-tailed deer, gray squirrel, and northern cardinal.
scenes.caption: Draw, print, or cut out ten animal cards. Label them with these names. Ruby-throated hummingbird, monarch butterfly, tundra swan, groundhog, and bat. Eastern box turtle, wood frog, white-tailed deer, gray squirrel, and northern cardinal.
scenes.visual: Ten simple, friendly animal cards deal onto the table one after another, each with a drawing and its name: ruby-throated hummingbird, monarch butterfly, tundra swan, groundhog, bat, eastern box turtle, wood frog, white-tailed deer, gray squirrel, northern cardinal.
scenes.narration: Draw, print, or cut out ten animal cards. Label them with these names. Ruby-throated hummingbird, monarch butterfly, tundra swan, groundhog, and bat. Eastern box turtle, wood frog, white-tailed deer, gray squirrel, and northern cardinal.

scenes.tts: Lay out the three sheets: Travel, Rest, and Stay and change. Let your child sort the cards with no help. Ask, 'How did you decide?' Write the reasons down, and don't correct anything yet.
scenes.caption: Lay out the three sheets: Travel, Rest, and Stay and change. Let your child sort the cards with no help. Ask, 'How did you decide?' Write the reasons down, and don't correct anything yet.
scenes.visual: Cards slide onto the three sheets, a few in surprising places. A speech bubble: 'How did you decide?' A small notepad collects short written lines. A calm label: 'No corrections yet'.
scenes.narration: Lay out the three sheets: Travel, Rest, and Stay and change. Let your child sort the cards with no help. Ask, 'How did you decide?' Write the reasons down, and don't correct anything yet.

scenes.tts: Now a question for you. Hummingbirds leave Virginia in fall, but cardinals stay all year. What do you predict is the main reason?
scenes.caption: Now a question for you. Hummingbirds leave Virginia in fall, but cardinals stay all year. What do you predict is the main reason?
scenes.visual: Split view on the table: the hummingbird card on the left, the cardinal card on the right, with a cold thermometer between them. Large question card at the top: 'Why does one leave and one stay?'
scenes.narration: Now a question for you. Hummingbirds leave Virginia in fall, but cardinals stay all year. What do you predict is the main reason?

scenes.visual: Hold the two cards and the question card. Subtle motion: snow keeps drifting past the window and the thermometer line trembles slightly.

scenes.tts: Cold matters, but food is a big reason. Hummingbirds eat nectar and insects, and those run out in a Virginia winter. So they travel to where food is. Cardinals stay all year and fluff their feathers in the cold.
scenes.caption: Cold matters, but food is a big reason. Hummingbirds eat nectar and insects, and those run out in a Virginia winter. So they travel to where food is. Cardinals stay all year and fluff their feathers in the cold.
scenes.visual: Behind the hummingbird card, flowers and small insects fade away under snow, and a dotted path leads south to a sunny, flowering place. The cardinal on the right fluffs its feathers on a bare branch. Label: 'Winter is hard: food runs short'.
scenes.narration: Cold matters, but food is a big reason. Hummingbirds eat nectar and insects, and those run out in a Virginia winter. So they travel to where food is. Cardinals stay all year and fluff their feathers in the cold.

scenes.tts: Use the guide’s animal list to check each card together. Ask, 'Where do you think this one goes?' Let your child move cards. Groundhogs hibernate in burrows. Deer grow a winter coat. Gray squirrels dig up buried nuts.
scenes.caption: Use the guide’s animal list to check each card together. Ask, 'Where do you think this one goes?' Let your child move cards. Groundhogs hibernate in burrows. Deer grow a winter coat. Gray squirrels dig up buried nuts.
scenes.visual: As the parent hears each example, show a groundhog curling up in a burrow on Rest, then a deer with a grayish winter coat and a gray squirrel digging up a buried nut on Stay and change. Keep the box turtle card visible on Rest with the turtle drawn beneath the soil.
scenes.narration: Use the guide’s animal list to check each card together. Ask, 'Where do you think this one goes?' Let your child move cards. Groundhogs hibernate in burrows. Deer grow a winter coat. Gray squirrels dig up buried nuts.

scenes.tts: When a card moves, ask, 'What made you change your mind?' Tundra swans are a fun surprise. They nest in the Arctic and fly thousands of miles south to spend winter here.
scenes.caption: When a card moves, ask, 'What made you change your mind?' Tundra swans are a fun surprise. They nest in the Arctic and fly thousands of miles south to spend winter here.
scenes.visual: A tundra swan card glides from the Rest sheet to the Travel sheet with a curved arrow. A simple map ribbon shows a long arrow from a snowy Arctic shore down to Virginia's rivers and bays. Speech bubble: 'What made you change your mind?'
scenes.narration: When a card moves, ask, 'What made you change your mind?' Tundra swans are a fun surprise. They nest in the Arctic and fly thousands of miles south to spend winter here.

scenes.tts: Sit at the window for fifteen minutes. Have your child predict how many kinds of birds you will see. Write down their guess. Tally the birds of each kind and note what they do. An empty yard is a result too.
scenes.caption: Sit at the window for fifteen minutes. Have your child predict how many kinds of birds you will see. Write down their guess. Tally the birds of each kind and note what they do. An empty yard is a result too.
scenes.visual: Back at the window. A timer shows '15 min'. Small birds land and hop; tally marks build on a sheet beside each drawn bird. A label: 'Empty yard? Still a result.'
scenes.narration: Sit at the window for fifteen minutes. Have your child predict how many kinds of birds you will see. Write down their guess. Tally the birds of each kind and note what they do. An empty yard is a result too.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child for the whole activity. Nobody touches a wild animal, alive or dead. Never touch a bat, even one that seems asleep or hurt. Bats can carry rabies.
scenes.caption: Stay with your child for the whole activity. Nobody touches a wild animal, alive or dead. Never touch a bat, even one that seems asleep or hurt. Bats can carry rabies.
scenes.visual: Calm safety badges appear by the window (no more than four): an adult and child side by side ('Stay together'), a crossed-out hand near a turtle ('Hands off wild animals'), a bat hanging with a crossed-out hand ('Never touch a bat').
scenes.narration: Stay with your child for the whole activity. Nobody touches a wild animal, alive or dead. Never touch a bat, even one that seems asleep or hurt. Bats can carry rabies.

scenes.tts: Leave resting turtles and frogs covered where you find them. Use a feeder only in winter. An adult handles it and washes hands after touching it or the seed. Keep birdseed away from children under four. If a child is choking, call nine one one.
scenes.caption: Leave resting turtles and frogs covered where you find them. Use a feeder only in winter. An adult handles it and washes hands after touching it or the seed. Keep birdseed away from children under four. If a child is choking, call nine one one.
scenes.visual: Leaves pile gently back over a sleeping turtle drawing. Then a feeder held by an adult's hands, and a crossed-out seed near a small face labelled 'Under 4: choking risk. Call 911'.
scenes.narration: Leave resting turtles and frogs covered where you find them. Use a feeder only in winter. An adult handles it and washes hands after touching it or the seed. Keep birdseed away from children under four. If a child is choking, call nine one one.

scenes.tts: Repeat the window watch in another season, at the same time of day. Compare the two sheets. Which kinds did you see both times? Which did you see only once? Think about what food was available in each season.
scenes.caption: Repeat the window watch in another season, at the same time of day. Compare the two sheets. Which kinds did you see both times? Which did you see only once? Think about what food was available in each season.
scenes.visual: The window scene shifts from snowy winter to green spring. Two tally sheets slide side by side; the cardinal appears on both, new birds appear only on the spring sheet. A small label: 'Who came? Who went?'
scenes.narration: Repeat the window watch in another season, at the same time of day. Compare the two sheets. Which kinds did you see both times? Which did you see only once? Think about what food was available in each season.

scenes.visual: End card over the window and yard. Large centered text: 'Winter food runs short: animals travel, rest, or stay and change.'
scenes.line: Winter food runs short: animals travel, rest, or stay and change.
